records.label: Kindred with four affected subjects
records.age_last: all died within four months after birth
records.segregation: segregation studies performed; homozygous variant identified as probable aetiology
quotes: We identified a kindred with four affected subjects presenting with a spectrum of findings including congenital arthrogryposis, no achievement of developmental milestones, early respiratory failure, neutropenia and recurrent infections. All died within four months after birth.
Exome sequencing identified a homozygous stop gain variant in SENP7 c.1474C>T; p.(Gln492*) as the probable aetiology.

records.label: 4 children from 3 unrelated families

variants.as_reported: rare, biallelic, specifically homozygous, loss of function variants in SENP7

quotes: identified rare, biallelic, specifically homozygous, loss of function variants in SENP7 in 4 children from 3 unrelated families presenting with neurodevelopmental abnormalities, dysmorphism, and immunodeficiency
Their clinical presentations were characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, intermittent neutropenia, and ultimately death in infancy for all 4 patients.

records.label: Consanguineous family with multiple affected members

variants.as_reported: recessive mutation in the highly conserved splice donor site

quotes: We report a consanguineous family with multiple affected members with AMC and identified a recessive mutation in the highly conserved splice donor site, resulting in the mis-splicing of the affected exons.

records.label: Consanguineous Egyptian family
quotes: a novel homozygous stop-gain variant in SENP7 c.745C>T; p.(Arg249*) in a consanguineous Egyptian family with a history of three fetal deaths, all presenting with multiple congenital anomalies
Similar anomalies were observed through ultrasound assessment of the current fetus, including arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, CNS malformations, congenital heart disease, and renal anomalies.

quotes: SENP7-Related Fatal Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita and Immunodeficiency: A Novel Missense Variation and Syndromic Delineation.

notes.statement: Pal et al. (2025) summarized the main clinical features and molecular findings of SENP7-associated disorder in previously reported cases and in their own patient, and described it as fatal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with immunodeficiency.
quotes: of prominent clinical features and molecular findings of SENP7-associated disorder in previous cases and our case.

notes.statement: Saad et al. (2025) identified a homozygous stop-gain variant in SENP7 (c.745C>T; p.Arg249*) by singleton exome sequencing of fetal DNA in a consanguineous Egyptian family with a lethal prenatal syndrome. The variant was predicted to produce a transcript degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, impairing SENP7 isopeptidase activity in deconjugating polySUMO chains.
quotes: Singleton exome sequencing (ES) of fetal DNA revealed a SENP7 variant allele, which results in a premature termination codon, and the mutant mRNA is predicted to be degraded by nonsense-mediated decay (NMD).
This leads to impaired gene function, particularly disrupting SENP7's isopeptidase activity in deconjugating polySUMO chains.

notes.statement: Kotecha et al. (2025) found a recessive variant at the highly conserved splice donor site of SENP7 in a consanguineous family with several members affected by lethal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita. The variant caused mis-splicing of the affected exons.
quotes: identified a recessive mutation in the highly conserved splice donor site, resulting in the mis-splicing of the affected exons
expanding the spectrum of SENP7 as a causative gene in rare cases of lethal AMC

notes.statement: Kotecha et al. (2025) noted that SENP7 is a deSUMOylase that is critical for sarcomere assembly and skeletal muscle contraction because it regulates the transcriptional program in skeletal muscle.
quotes: SENP7 is a deSUMOylase that is critical for sarcomere assembly and skeletal muscle contraction by regulating the transcriptional program in the skeletal muscle.

notes.statement: Kobayashi et al. (2024) noted that SENP7 is a sentrin-specific protease involved in deSUMOylation of proteins essential for cell regulation, and proposed that deficiency of deSUMOylation may represent a novel mechanism of primary immunodeficiency.
quotes: SENP7 is a sentrin-specific protease involved in posttranslational modification of proteins essential for cell regulation, via a process referred to as deSUMOylation.
We propose that deficiency of deSUMOylation may represent a novel mechanism of primary immunodeficiency.

notes.statement: Samra et al. (2023) found decreased SENP7 mRNA expression in fibroblasts from the proband, with significant protein dysregulation in total cell lysates and chromatin fraction, and reduced levels of HP1-alpha, different histones, and H3K9me3. They suggested that loss of SENP7 leads to reduced heterochromatin condensation and subsequent aberrant gene expression.
quotes: The proband's fibroblasts demonstrated decreased mRNA expression. Protein expression studies showed significant protein dysregulation in total cell lysates and in the chromatin fraction.
We found that HP1α levels as well as different histones and H3K9me3 were reduced in patient fibroblasts.
suggest loss of SENP7 leads to reduced heterochromatin condensation and subsequent aberrant gene expression.
